question: What is the minimum distance between centers of two circles having radii 5 cm and 3 cm such that exactly three common tangents exist?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Two circles will have exactly three common tangents only when they touch each other externally.

When circles touch externally, the distance between their centers is exactly equal to the sum of their radii.

Distance = r₁ + r₂ = 5 + 3 = 8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of first circle (r₁) = 5 cm

Radius of second circle (r₂) = 3 cm

Number of common tangents = 3

 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 5 cm 3 cm C1 C2 Distance between centers = 8 cm 

**Concept Used:**

The total number of common tangents depends on the distance between the centers (d) relative to the sum and difference of their radii.

For exactly 3 common tangents to exist, the two circles must touch each other externally.

Condition for externally touching circles: Distance (d) = r₁ + r₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance between centers = r₁ + r₂

⇒ Distance = 5 cm + 3 cm

⇒ Distance = 8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Externally Touching Circles

When distance d = r₁ + r₂, the circles touch externally. Exactly 3 common tangents can be drawn (2 direct, 1 transverse).

Intersecting Circles

When |r₁ − r₂| r₁ + r₂, the circles are far apart. Exactly 4 common tangents can be drawn (2 direct, 2 transverse).
